core.title: Derive components from the feature's ioSeeds and WMBT verbs
core.given: A feature's components are being planned, whatever ioSeeds (consume/produce) or WMBTs the feature currently has, including none
core.when: the planner generates, adds or re-derives that feature's components
core.then: Derive each component from a concrete ioSeed trigger or WMBT verb in the feature, with the business capability and layer the derivation map gives that trigger.
prefer: Steps: analyze ioSeeds/WMBTs → identify needed capabilities → assign layers → generate up to 8 components with complete structure → confirm all feature needs are covered.

ioSeeds map: produce event:*/notification:* → event publishing (application|integration); consume event:*/notification:* → event handling (application|integration); consume command:* → command processing (application); produce query:* → query handling (application|domain).

WMBT verbs map: validate/verify/check → validator (domain); process/compute/calculate → processor (application|domain); display/show/render → display (presentation); store/save/persist → persister (integration); coordinate/orchestrate/manage → coordinator (application).
Where the map allows two layers (a|b), either listed layer complies; no tie-breaker is prescribed, so record which trigger justified the chosen layer.

If the feature has neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs, or covering every trigger would need more than 8 components, report that conflict instead of inventing components, exceeding the cap or silently dropping coverage.
avoid: Inventing a component with no ioSeed or WMBT trigger behind it.
More than 8 components for one feature.
Leaving an ioSeed trigger or WMBT need uncovered.
core.why: Deriving components from ioSeeds and WMBTs keeps generation systematic and traceable: every component exists because a concrete trigger in the feature called for it.
evidence: Each planned component can be traced to an ioSeed entry or WMBT verb of the feature.
Each component's business capability and layer match the derivation map entry for its trigger.
The feature has at most 8 components.
Every ioSeed trigger and WMBT need of the feature is covered by at least one component.
A feature with neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs has no derived components; any component listed for it is a finding.
verification: Check scope: read one feature's plan — its ioSeeds (consume/produce), its WMBTs and its component list — and verify each component traces to a concrete ioSeed entry or WMBT verb, and that its business capability and layer match the derivation-map entry for that trigger.

The same check verifies the per-feature cap (at most 8 components, each with complete structure) and full coverage (every ioSeed trigger and WMBT need covered by at least one component); when covering every trigger would exceed the cap, the expected outcome is a reported conflict, not silent truncation or invention.
Applicability does not depend on triggers being present: for a feature with neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs, every listed component is untriggered and therefore a finding.
Where the derivation map allows two layers, either listed layer complies; the check enforces only that the justifying trigger is recorded, with no tie-breaker between the two layers.

Enforcement is review-based: the reference realization prescribes no automated detector for this rule (implementation type 'none'); the scope above is what a reviewer — or a future validator — checks.

fires: Planner generates the component list for a feature that has ioSeeds, WMBTs, or both.
Planner generates components for a feature that has only WMBTs (no ioSeeds), or only ioSeeds (no WMBTs).
Planner is asked to generate or add components for a feature that has neither ioSeeds nor WMBTs: the rule fires and any component without a trigger is rejected as invented.
Planner adds a new component to an existing feature plan.
Planner revises a feature's WMBTs or ioSeeds and re-derives its existing components.
doesNotFire: Planner edits a feature's description or acceptance wording without touching components, ioSeeds or WMBTs.
Coder implements an already-planned component in code.
Planner authors wagon-level docs that list no components.

profileRequirements.meaning: The layer roles the derivation map assigns components to. The core names layers by canonical role (domain, application, integration, presentation); the profile supplies the stack's actual layer roles and their local names, so the map can be applied and checked in that stack.
profileRequirements.bunValue: presentation, application, domain, integration — the four layer roles named by the derivation maps (prefer[1]: application|integration, application, application|domain; prefer[2]: domain, application|domain, presentation, integration, application)

bunOnly.text: Examples: WMBT 'persist choice' → ChoicePersister at integration; ioSeeds.consume has command:* → command-processing component at application.
bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked example that names a specific component ('ChoicePersister'); its role-level content is the derivation map in core:prefer[1]/core:prefer[2]. The concrete example is delivered by bun.json itself as the reference example.

bunOnly.reason: Concrete worked examples belong to the reference realization; the counter-example's neutral form is core:avoid[0] and the example's role-level content is core:prefer[1]/core:prefer[2].

neutralityNotes: This rule governs planning artifacts (features, ioSeeds, WMBTs, component lists) and its agent-facing text names no stack, runtime, framework, file suffix or path, so given/when/then/why, the two derivation maps, the cap, the coverage obligation, the evidence list and the activation block (facts, fires, doesNotFire) are carried essentially verbatim. Layer names in the maps are the canonical roles domain/application/integration/presentation and bind to a concrete stack only through roles.layers (the sole profile requirement). ioSeeds, WMBT, wagon and the trigger vocabularies (event:*/notification:*/command:*/query:* prefixes and the WMBT verb lists), plus the per-feature cap of 8, are ATDD methodology content, not stack facts, so they stay in the core. The only realization-specific content is (a) the concrete worked examples (prefer[3], verifier_detail[3], the examples half of verifier_detail[4]), kept in bun.json because it is delivered as the worked reference example, and (b) the term/step ids of verifier_detail[0..2] (from_io_seeds, from_wmbt_analysis, generation_strategy, mapping_example and sub-ids), which are detector/term identifiers of this one realization. Activation fact notes were dropped per the neutral schema; their content survives in fires/doesNotFire and verification.
